A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Segment Policy Optimization work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including content relocated between versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original SPO training and evaluation results on GSM8K, MATH500 and AIME24, alongside ablations and appendix experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds evaluations with further Qwen models, Knights-and-Knaves and a masked-GRPO comparison.

M1.justification: SPO-chain and SPO-tree retain their segmentation strategies, Monte Carlo estimators, probability masks, optimization objectives and replay buffer. Algorithm 1 is unchanged apart from typesetting. The additional evaluations introduce no documented procedure change.

E1.justification: V2 Appendix F adds the three-person Knights-and-Knaves subset, testing identity deduction from truthful and false statements. This adds one narrowly defined non-mathematical task to the retained GSM8K, MATH/MATH500 and AIME24 coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 5(a) adds GRPO with probability masks to the long-CoT MATH500 comparison, where v1 Figure 6(a) compared only SPO-tree and vanilla GRPO. Masked GRPO already appeared in the short-CoT ablation; its participation in this corresponding long-CoT comparison is new.

E3.justification: V2 adds configurations using Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B. The granularity study changes from test accuracy versus iterations to validation accuracy versus hours, and Knights-and-Knaves reports test reward. Existing hyperparameter tables remain unchanged; these additions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new long-CoT masked-GRPO control tests whether masking alone explains SPO-tree's advantage. The granularity analysis now examines accuracy against elapsed time. Existing partition-strategy, tree-structure, normalization and qualitative case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or experimental error bars. The added result curves do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 Figure 11 substantially expands reported results with three Qwen mathematical-reasoning comparisons and a Knights-and-Knaves test-reward comparison, showing SPO-tree ahead of GRPO. Figure 5(a) adds the masked-GRPO curve, which remains below SPO-tree. Granularity results are replaced by validation/time curves, not same-setting accuracy gains. Table 1 and the original 56.7% SPO-chain GSM8K result remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The MDP assumptions, segment-advantage definition, cutpoint optimization and appendix derivations are retained. The GRPO background is abbreviated into prose, and existing masks receive explicit indicator notation, without changing the mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains critic-free segment-level credit assignment through SPO-chain and SPO-tree. Both abstracts retain the same claimed 6–12 percentage-point GSM8K and 7–11 percentage-point MATH500 improvements. Rewritten contribution and conclusion passages preserve their substantive scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix G explains that on-policy constraints limit how far tree samples can be deferred through the replay buffer. V2 also distinguishes interval 5's time-efficiency advantage from interval 2's slightly higher final accuracy, and qualifies PPO overhead by acknowledging critic heads rather than asserting necessarily doubled costs.

D1.justification: The explicit Open R1 evaluation-code URL in v1's bibliography is omitted from v2 reference [8], slightly reducing access information. The SPO repository link, pseudocode, hardware disclosures and five hyperparameter tables remain unchanged. The new experiments receive no corresponding detailed parameter tables.

R1.justification: V2 adds Xie et al.'s work on memorization in logical reasoning for Knights-and-Knaves. The main positioning relative to PPO, GRPO, VinePPO and process-reward approaches remains substantially unchanged. Most other reference edits update formatting or publication metadata.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: detailed related work moves to Appendix A, Background combines preliminary material with focused comparisons, method subsections become inline numbered components, and the two experimental subsections become separate sections. Appendices are reordered, several explanatory passages are condensed or rewritten, and acknowledgments are added.

P2.justification: V2 adds the four-panel Figure 11, replaces the granularity subplot's axes and curves, and adds a masked-GRPO curve and legend entry. The introductory overfitting figure moves to the appendix, DeepSeekMath plots are arranged side by side, and Table 1 more visibly separates differently trained comparators. Most existing displays are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the evidence through additional model evaluations, a non-mathematical task and a long-CoT control separating masking from segment-level advantages. The time-based granularity analysis and explicit replay-buffer limitation improve interpretation. These are useful but limited gains: the new experiments lack detailed reproducibility settings and uncertainty estimates, while the central method and original headline results remain unchanged.
